ai.description: Wall’s Cat Snake reaches 1.2 meters. It is pale brown with dark, jagged crossbands and a distinct, dark postocular stripe. A slender, nocturnal colubrid, it features a triangular head and vertical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga walli* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark, V-shaped or chevron-like markings on the nape, which differ from the patterns found in other Indian cat snakes.
ai.habitat: Wall's Cat Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Wall's Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours navigating tree branches and rocky crevices in search of geckos and other small prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: Boiga walli is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–11 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with eggs often deposited in tree hollows or crevices.
ai.distributionRemarks: Boiga walli is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily found in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
